channel.title: Merkle Street
channel.description: Merkle Street reports crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, layer 2s, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation, security incidents and protocol upgrades.

item.title: Why Ethereum Is the Source Chain for Mantle Bridge Deposits
item.description: For a canonical Mantle transfer, Ethereum is the source chain; choose it when the asset, settlement path, timing and fee budget fit your business controls.

item.title: Mantle Bridge: Check Which Token Will Arrive
item.description: A bridge can move an asset across networks or route it through a swap. Check the destination token and contract before signing, because a ticker alone does not identify what arrives.

item.title: How wrapped bitcoin works on Ethereum
item.description: Wrapped bitcoin gives BTC an ERC-20 form on Ethereum, backed by reserves but dependent on an issuer, a redemption route and market demand to hold its price near BTC.

item.title: Starknet opens vote on studying an independent post-quantum chain
item.description: Starknet opened a seven-day, nonbinding STRK poll on researching an independent post-quantum Layer 1, a first step that would not approve leaving Ethereum.

item.title: Why Treasury Must Compare Net Value Before Bridging
item.description: Treasury should compare what arrives after bridge fees, swaps, slippage and destination costs, because the amount sent is not the amount available to use.

item.title: Why Bitcoin Becomes a Token on Another Chain
item.description: Wrapped Bitcoin works with another chain’s apps because a bridge holds BTC and issues a matching token, whose redemption depends on the bridge working.

item.title: How to Swap Into Collateral for a Remote Lending Market
item.description: To use a remote lending market, move an accepted asset to its chain, swap if needed, then supply it to the market contract before borrowing against it.

item.title: Why a BSC-to-Arbitrum Swap Needs Gas on Both Chains
item.description: A BSC-to-Arbitrum stablecoin transfer can stall before or after the swap if gas is missing: keep BNB for BSC and ETH for Arbitrum, and verify the route.

item.title: Why Cross-Chain Swaps Take Longer Than the Quote
item.description: A cross-chain swap waits on source-chain confirmation, a bridge or relayer, and destination execution; the quote estimates a route, not a guaranteed arrival time.

item.title: Why RenJS Integrators Must Persist Deposit State
item.description: RenJS deposits cross chains and wait for confirmations, signatures and minting; saved state lets an app resume, reconcile and explain each transfer reliably.

item.title: Why a Monero Bridge Transfer Can Stay Pending
item.description: A Monero bridge transfer can wait at XMR confirmation, bridge processing, or destination settlement; check each stage before resending or opening a support case.

item.title: Solana sets Oct. 21 for Alpenglow consensus switch
item.description: Solana scheduled Alpenglow for Oct. 21, targeting 150-millisecond finality by changing how validators certify blocks, a shift that could speed payment guarantees.

item.title: Fairshake backs 32 House candidates after crypto bill stalls
item.description: Fairshake named 32 House incumbents for midterm support, including six getting $1 million each, after the Senate blocked the crypto market-structure bill.

item.title: How a Mantle bridge transfer works, and how to check it arrived
item.description: A Mantle bridge transfer starts on one chain and completes on another. Check the source transaction, destination address and token balance to confirm arrival.

item.title: How to use thor swap from your own wallet
item.description: A wallet-led thor swap starts with the source chain, destination asset and recipient address; the wallet signs the transfer while the route handles the cross-chain exchange.

item.title: Binance sets Nov. 10 cutoff for mining pool services
item.description: Binance will close its mining pool and linked services on Nov. 10, ending mining credits at the cutoff and requiring users to move rigs and settle open positions.

item.title: Ledger Ties Confirmed Wallet Drains to CryptoBilis Reseller
item.description: Ledger says every confirmed drain in the Oct. 9 incident involved CryptoBilis-sold devices, but it has not disclosed customer losses or how the hardware was altered.

item.title: XRPL defends emergency fix for XRP overflow bug
item.description: XRPL developers say an emergency server patch stopped an order book overflow flaw that could create spendable XRP, bypassing the usual validator vote.

item.title: Samsung Wallet to add USDC remittances for 82M devices
item.description: Samsung will add USDC transfers to Wallet for eligible US Galaxy users in late October, routing money to crypto wallets or bank accounts in over 60 countries.

item.title: ESMA opens inquiry into tokenised collateral for EU clearing
item.description: ESMA is asking market participants how tokenised collateral could work at EU clearing houses, testing whether existing safeguards can cover its risks.
